x: We had a new innovation with a 120 Yards Low Hurdles handicap, and John Briggs the scratch man was just beaten by Les Christmas with Peter Hunt in third place.

This was won by Alan Law, who just beat John Briggs, with Frank Kemp a close third. The 3 miles walk saw the field start off their time allowances and Joe Wilson, who went off the limit mark, set a good strong pace and was never headed.

In the 2 miles walk we saw our old friend Colin Sutton getting among the prizes once again and his trip abroad has evidently not impaired his speed. We put on a 120 Hurdles event, but this only drew three competitors and John Briggs just failed to catch his limit man.

One or two other members spoke on the subject and John Briggs, one of our junior members, was most emphatic in a short but well-presented speech, that the Club was good value and most worthy of the greater subscription.

It was very pleasing to see John Briggs come all the way from Liverpool to compete in the Club Hurdles Championship. Our younger members are progressing very rapidly, in particular Choate, Strang and Windley are all doing well.
